correctness.rationale: Full semilinear order with definable C is homogeneous (Bodirsky et al. 2014 Sections 2-3.1); every upward old-antichain type corresponds to exactly one clade of the finite rooted binary tree. Ordered distinct clade pairs uniquely determine all (<,C) diagrams, except equal clades allow the two strict orders. The counts are 2n(2n-1) in total and ancestor-pair count H in each strict-order channel; the induction H=2S+1 closes the proof for all n>=1. A separate explicit finite-diagram checker enumerates every shape up to eight leaves, including C-signatures and both same-edge orders. Finite checks are corroboration, not the infinite argument.

value.rationale: The union of principal upper cones over a named antichain is a canonical definable positive region in an existentially closed semilinear order. Its total unary and binary type counts are shape-blind, but comparing the strict-order and incomparability pair-type channels recovers the rooted tree Sackin balance index. The theorem gives a sharp earliest tree-size separation and exact classical extremal geometry. The model-theoretic bridge is motivated and structurally interpretable, not an arbitrary numerical slice; it does not claim the classical tree-balance extrema are new.
